collection.source_input: US9372336B2, the prescription table transcribed in this batch's brief (the brief's table 1 of 11; the publication's own Example 1): a surface table with eight numbered surfaces in ne and νe and a D/2 column, from the object plane at 15.0000 mm through the aperture stop at surface 2 to the image plane at surface 8
collection.redistribution: public patent document; the prescription numbers are transcribed as facts, no source asset is redistributed
collection.attribution: US9372336B2, Olympus Corporation; the design is cited by publication number and example

title: Endoscope objective optical system, US9372336B2 example 1

design.source_reference: US9372336B2 example 1 (the brief's prescription table 1 of 11, which is page order and also the publication's own Example 1). The mapping is confirmed, not assumed: the publication's TABLE 1 of conditional expressions gives Example 1 as fF/fR 0.257, Φc*fR 1.000, L/f 2.695, Ih/f 0.778, Hm 0.642 and DR/2 0.81, and this surface table is the one that produces them (its rear-group D/2 is 0.81 and its spacings sum to 2.6946 mm)

aperture_validity.basis: The native Project clips the axial cone at L1/S2 with a 0.091327 mm clear radius at the coincident mask plane.
aperture_validity.consequence: The clear aperture clips rays at the refracting interface. A downstream paraxial image in air is unconfirmed.
aperture_validity.satisfaction_basis: no separate blocking plate is modelled and this batch asserts no stop-dependent evidence

spectrum.sampling_wavelengths_basis: SOURCE_STATED air wavelength 546.074 nm (the e line, the wavelength the table's ne and νe refer to), converted once to vacuum with the engine's own air model (6432.8 / 2949810 / 25540, material_physics.air_index_exact): 546.2231601210934 nm
spectrum.wavelength_precision: full precision as used by the Project; rounded values in this document are for display only

sampling_span_nm.note: the source states ne and νe only, so the Project is evaluated at the e line alone. A zero-width interval cannot be filtered, so the span is a +/-0.5 nm window around that one sample; it is a numerical convenience, not a second wavelength and not a measured band

continuous_coverage_nm.note: the source states no operating wavelength range; an ne/νe pair does not establish continuous coverage

effective_focal_length_mm.definition: Signed paraxial effective focal length of the native Project.

back_focal_length_mm.definition: Signed paraxial distance from the last optical surface vertex to the rear focal point for collimated input.

total_track_mm.definition: Axial distance from the first optical surface to the image plane.

engine_check.method: thick-lens paraxial ABCD through the committed Project's COMPOUND unit

comparison.rule: per quantity: |engine - source| <= atol + rtol * scale, with scale = |EFL| for the effective focal length and max(|BFL|, |EFL|) for the back focal length. atol = 0.005 mm is half a unit in the last decimal of the coarsest focal length these publications print (two decimals); rtol = 2e-3 is 1e-3 for a prescription printed to four decimals on radii as small as 0.27 mm plus 1e-3 for the engine's air-referenced index convention

effective_focal_length.basis: the source states no such first-order value

back_focal_length.basis: the source states no such first-order value

comparison.why: the publication states neither an effective focal length nor a back focal length for this example, so the two-quantity rule has no pair to judge. The engine's values are recorded under engine_check as ENGINE_COMPUTED facts and no verdict is claimed

nominal_effective_focal_length_mm.note: the publication states no effective focal length in millimetres. Its TABLE 1 of conditional expressions prints ratios only (Ih/f 0.778, L/f 2.695) and the miscellaneous data prints Ih = 0.778 mm, so the design is normalised to f = 1.000 mm; that is a derived design target, not a measured focal length, and it is not used as a comparison value

nominal_back_focal_length_mm.definition: from the last surface vertex to the paraxial image point

f_number.definition: image-space f-number as the publication states it (the miscellaneous data table of example 1: F/5.674)
f_number.basis: SOURCE_STATED (the publication's miscellaneous data table for example 1)
f_number.note: The native Project clips the axial cone at L1/S2 with a 0.091327 mm clear radius at the coincident mask plane. The aperture calculator leaves the finite conjugate f-number unconfirmed because the axial focus lies at the final interface.

field.definition: the publication's miscellaneous data table states W = 46.11, read here as a half angle of view
field.basis: SOURCE_STATED (the publication's miscellaneous data table for example 1: W = 46.11)
field.convention_note: the extracted miscellaneous table for examples 1-3 carries a stray leading digit on some numeric cells (it prints 'Ih = 40.778' and 'Hm = 40.642' where the publication's own conditional table gives Ih/f = 0.778 at f = 1 mm and Hm = 0.642), so 'W = 46.11' is read with that caveat. As a half angle of 46.11 deg it is consistent with the stated image height of 0.778 mm at a 1.0006 mm focal length only with about 25 % barrel distortion, which is ordinary for a wide-angle endoscope objective; read as a full field of 146.11 deg (half 73.06 deg) it would need about 76 % barrel distortion, which no design of this class shows. The value is recorded as a half angle and the alternative reading is left open rather than resolved by assumption

model_glasses.name: G151633
model_glasses.basis: the source states ne 1.51633 and νe 64.14 only (e-line data); two numbers do not define a dispersion curve, so the material is a constant index at the stated ne and no dispersion is claimed. Used on surfaces 1 and 5

model_glasses.name: G172916
model_glasses.basis: the source states ne 1.72916 and νe 54.68 only (e-line data); constant index at the stated ne, no dispersion claimed

model_glasses.name: G188300
model_glasses.basis: the source states ne 1.88300 and νe 40.76 only (e-line data); constant index at the stated ne, no dispersion claimed

model_glasses.name: G152274
model_glasses.basis: the source states ne 1.52274 and νe 55.00 only (e-line data); constant index at the stated ne, no dispersion claimed. The last plane-parallel element, whose back face is the source's image plane

materials.policy: Every glass is a constant index at the source's stated ne. The table gives ne and νe only, which cannot define a dispersion curve; fitting one would invent a material. The νe values are recorded as source_stated_vd because the record contract names the field that way, and the basis of each entry states that the number is an e-line Abbe number. Published catalog glasses were compared as a cross-check (catalog_comparisons) and never substituted.

catalog_comparisons.note: cross-check only, not substituted. The catalog values are d-line; the source's are e-line, so the agreement of the d-line pair is a coincidence of the catalogue's own data, not evidence about the source's e-line numbers

cross-check only, not substituted. No catalog glass matches this pair closely; the nearest is a borosilicate sheet glass, consistent with the element being the cover plate whose back face is the source's image plane

approximations.detail: every glass is a constant index at the source's stated ne; the source's νe is recorded but no dispersion curve is modelled, so axial colour and chromatic focal shift are not represented
the Project is evaluated at the e line only
The native Project clips the axial cone at L1/S2 with a 0.091327 mm clear radius at the coincident mask plane.

the source's last surface (surface 8) is the back face of a plane plate and is also its image plane, so the source's own image space is glass. The format requires an air image space, so a zero-spacing plane surface is added at the same vertex; the added medium is 0 mm of air, so the optical path and every first-order value are unchanged

the source states an object distance of 15.0000 mm; the Project places its source there, so the record is finite-conjugate. The paraxial image for that conjugate lands within 3e-5 mm of the source's image plane at 2.6946 mm
nominal prescription surfaces; no figure, centring or surface-roughness error is modelled

notes: project check accepted the committed Project with os-optics 0.14.0

project solids reported no error-severity finding; its only finding is an INFO on the 1.88300 element's edge thickness relative to its clear diameter, which follows from the source's own 0.63 mm centre thickness on a 1.62 mm clear diameter

paraxial is NOT_CHECKED, not MATCHED: the publication states no effective focal length or back focal length in millimetres, only the ratios Ih/f and L/f. The engine's 1.000598 mm EFL lands 0.06 % above the normalised f = 1.000 mm design target, outside the 1e-5 + 1e-4*scale rule, and no BFL is stated at all

the transcription is self-consistent with the source: the transcribed spacings sum to 2.6946 mm, the publication states L/f = 2.695 at f = 1 mm, the engine reports the image plane at 2.6946 mm, and the paraxial image for the stated 15.0000 mm object distance lands within 3e-5 mm of it

the clear semi-diameters are the source's stated D/2 values used verbatim, not derived: the column prints one value per element on the row where it changes, so 0.55 mm applies to surfaces 1, 3 and 4, 0.81 mm to surfaces 5 and 6, and 0.89 mm to surfaces 7 and 8, each edged 0.02 mm larger. Only the stop plate and the merged stop are approximations

the source's stop has a zero thickness against surface 3, so no blocking plate is modelled: the record is STOP_NOT_BLOCKING and not eligible for stop-dependent evaluation, and the stated F/5.674 is recorded as a source fact rather than reproduced by the geometry
no field verification: this batch built no per-field configurations, so no field-dependent quantity is asserted

record_hash_method: SHA-256 over this record's JSON with the record_hash and record_hash_method members removed: json.dumps(..., sort_keys=True, ensure_ascii=False) encoded as UTF-8, no trailing newline. Recompute it from the committed record.json after parsing the JSON, not from the file's bytes.
